newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Industry ministers to discuss EU competiveness.
newsitem.headline: Industry ministers to discuss EU competiveness.

text.p: European Union industry ministers will discuss the bloc's global competitiveness at an informal gathering in February, Dutch Economic Affairs Minister Hans Wijers said on Monday.
In a letter to parliament outlining economic priorities for the Dutch presidency of the EU which begins on January 1, Wijers said he would host the meeting in The Hague on February 1 and 2.
The industry ministers would consider the implications for competitiveness of attempts to create a single market across all 15 eu member states, he said.
Wijers said the informal meeting would pay particular attention to the competitive position of Europe's information and communication technology (ICT) sector.

"This sector is the motor behind the information society and is of great importance to Europe. But we have to acknowledge that the European ICT sector is losing ground to competitors in the United States, Japan and Korea," he said.
Wijers said the creation of a single EU market for natural gas would top the agenda of EU energy ministers meeting in Brussels on May 26.

Ministers had already reached agreement under the Irish presidency on several important principles and there was broad agreement, for example, that public service commitments should be imposed on gas companies, he said.

Wijers said the Netherlands would also give priority during its tenure of the EU presidency to implementing decisions reached at the inaugural ministerial meeting of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) earlier this month.
This would include the conclusion of negotiations on an agreement for free trade in information technology, he said.
